newsitem.title: USA: US Democrat group offers 0.8 pct CPI cut in budget.
newsitem.headline: US Democrat group offers 0.8 pct CPI cut in budget.

text.p: A coalition of moderate to conservative Democrats Wednesday released a budget proposal that included a 0.8 percent downward adjustment for federal programs indexed to the consumer price index.

The group, known as the "Blue Dog" Democrats released an outline of their budget proposal which they said would balance the budget by 2002 and did not include any tax cuts. The group of 22 lawmakers said tax cuts should be dealt with separate from the budget so it is clear what would pay for them.
The plan would not reduce the official measurement of CPI, but adjust the indexation of programs based on it, they said.
The coalition said its plan would achieve $103.7 billion in savings over five years from the CPI-related adjustment.
If the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics changes its calculation of the CPI, the magnitude of the adjustment could be reduced, the group said.
A report prepared by a commission chaired by economist Michael Boskin late last year said the CPI overstated inflation by 1.1 percentage points.
Republicans have said they want President Clinton to take the lead on any proposals to change CPI. Programs linked to the measure include Social Security and veterans benefits.
